followUps: Did you return it in good condition?
p3: What kinds of things do people often borrow from friends?
Why might some people be unwilling to lend their belongings, even to friends?
Is it a good idea to lend money to friends?
What are the benefits of sharing things like tools in a community?
How popular are sharing schemes, like bike rentals, in your country?
Do you think people will own fewer things and share more in the future?

title: Describe a household appliance that makes your life easier.
explain: and explain how it makes your life easier.
followUps: Who uses it most in your home?
p3: Who does most of the housework in homes in your country?
Should children be expected to help with household chores? From what age?
How have household appliances changed family life since your grandparents' time?
Which appliance would be hardest for people to live without?
Would you say people replace their appliances more often than they need to?
Do you think robots will do most housework in the future?

title: Describe something you are saving up to buy.
bullets: how you found out about it
explain: and explain why you want to buy it.
followUps: How long will it take you to save for it?
p3: What do young people in your country usually save money for?
Why do some people find it difficult to save money?
Do you think it is better to save up or to borrow money for something you want?
What methods do advertisers use to persuade people to buy things they don't need?
Should advertising aimed at young children be more strictly controlled? Why?
Does owning more possessions really make people happier? Why or why not?

title: Describe a musical instrument you would like to learn.
bullets: where you have heard it played
explain: and explain what draws you to this instrument.
followUps: Do you know anyone who plays this instrument?
p3: Which musical instruments do children in your country usually learn?
Should all children learn to play an instrument at school?
Why is it that so many people give up learning an instrument?
How does traditional music in your country differ from modern music?
In what ways can music bring people from different backgrounds together?
Do you think traditional instruments will still be played in the future?

title: Describe a website you often visit.
explain: and explain why you find this website useful.
followUps: Is there anything about this website you would change?
p3: Which websites do people in your country use most, apart from social media?
How can people tell if information online is reliable?
Are news websites as trustworthy as printed newspapers, in your view?
Do you think online courses can be as effective as classes in person?
Has the internet brought people closer together or made them more isolated?
Should children be allowed to use the internet without supervision?
